summary: Defines a Telnet option that lets a client tell the server where the user is located. It is a small extension to Telnet.

plainLanguage.summary: SEND-LOCATION lets a user's Telnet program offer the user's location to the server. If the server accepts, the user side can send the location as printable text.

questions: how does telnet send user location
what is the telnet send-location option
how does telnet send a location
subtitle: A Telnet option for sending a user's location to the server.

tldr.problem: Logged-in user listings may show only the originating site for a person connected over the network.
tldr.mechanism: The user Telnet offers the option, and after the server accepts, sends the location as printable ASCII in a subnegotiation.
tldr.outcome: A server that can use the information can display the user's location as well as the originating site.

today: RFC 779 is a Proposed Standard. The unit metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it.

sections.title: Why Send a Location
sections.content:
Some sites list people who are logged in, with their names and locations. For a user connected through the network, the location may identify only the site they came from.

The option lets the user's Telnet program provide the user's location so the server can display it alongside the site name. The RFC notes that SUPDUP already has this function.
sections.plainLanguage: A network login may identify the connecting site but not where the user is. This option can provide that extra location detail.

sections.title: The SEND-LOCATION Commands
sections.content:
The option name is SEND-LOCATION and its code is 23. IAC WILL requests or agrees to send the location; IAC DO requests or agrees that the other side send it. The WON'T and DON'T forms refuse or prohibit its use.

The default is WON'T SEND-LOCATION and DON'T SEND-LOCATION, so location data is not sent unless the option is negotiated.
sections.plainLanguage: The Telnet sides first agree whether to use the option. Until they do, the location is not sent.

sections.title: Sending the Location
sections.content:
The location is sent in a subnegotiation: IAC SB SEND-LOCATION <location> IAC SE. The location is a sequence of printable ASCII characters and ends with IAC SE.

When the user Telnet knows the location, it should offer to send it with IAC WILL SEND-LOCATION. A server able to use the information answers IAC DO SEND-LOCATION; the user Telnet may then send it at any time.
sections.plainLanguage: After the server agrees, the user side can send the location as readable text inside a Telnet subnegotiation.
